title: Denying the Correlative
description: Introducing alternatives when, in fact, there are none.  This could happen when you have two mutually exclusive statements (*correlative conjunction*) presented as choices, and instead of picking one or the other, introduce a third -- usually as  a distraction from having to choose between the two alternatives presented.
logical_form:
Either X or not X.

Therefore, Y.

examples.example:
Rocco:  Do ya have the five grand you owe me or not?

Paulie: I can get it.

Rocco: That means you don’t have it?

Paulie: I know someone who does.

Rocco: Read my lips: do you have my money or not?

Paulie: No.

(sound of a baseball bat breaking kneecaps)
examples.explanation:
Rocco was asking a simple question, and out of personal safety, Paulie was committing the fallacy of *denying the correlative* by offering up another option to a choice that only had two.  If Paulie were smarter, he could not have committed the fallacy and saved his kneecaps, by honesty and a little negotiation:

Rocco:  Do ya have the five grand you owe me or not?

Paulie: No. I realize I did not hold up my end of the deal, so I will compensate you for that.

Rocco: What are you sayin’?

Paulie: I can have your $5000 by this time tomorrow, plus an extra $500 for making you have to wait an extra day.

Rocco: Deal.  I’ll be back this time tomorrow.

(sound of heart dropping from throat)

examples.example:
Judge: So did you kill your landlord or not?

Kirk: I fought with him.
examples.explanation: Here is a classic case where a “yes” or “no” answer is expected, and the only acceptable answer to such a question, yet Kirk is deflecting the question by providing a third answer option, that leaves the original question unanswered.

exceptions: When non-mutually exclusive choices are presented as mutually exclusive choices, the fallacy lies with the one presenting the choices (*[false dilemma](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/False-Dilemma)* ).
tips: Don’t borrow money from anyone named "Rocco."
references: This a logical fallacy frequently used on the Internet. No academic sources could be found.
description_et: Alternatiivide tutvustamine, kui neid tegelikult pole.  See võib juhtuda siis, kui teil on kaks üksteist välistavat väidet (*korrelatiivne konjunktsioon*) valikuna ja selle asemel, et valida üks või teine, tutvustage kolmandat – tavaliselt selleks, et juhtida tähelepanu kõrvale kahe esitatud alternatiivi vahel valiku tegemisest.
logical_form_et:
Kas X või mitte X.

Seetõttu Y.
exceptions_et: Kui üksteist välistavad valikud esitatakse üksteist välistavate valikutena, on eksitus valikute esitajal (*[vale dilemma](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/False-Dilemma)*).

examples_et.example:
Rocco: Kas teil on viis tuhat, mis olete mulle võlgu, või mitte?

Paulie: Ma saan selle.

Rocco: See tähendab, et teil pole seda?

Paulie: Ma tean kedagi, kes seda teeb.

Rocco: Lugege mu huulilt: kas teil on mu raha või mitte?

Paulie: Ei.

(sound of a baseball bat breaking kneecaps)
examples_et.explanation:
Rocco esitas lihtsa küsimuse ja isikliku ohutuse huvides tegi Paulie eksituse, *eitades korrelatiivi*, pakkudes valikule, millel oli ainult kaks, teist võimalust.  Kui Paulie oleks targem, poleks ta aususe ja väikese läbirääkimise teel saanud eksimust teha ja päästa oma põlvekedrad:

Rocco: Kas teil on viis tuhat, mis olete mulle võlgu, või mitte?

Paulie: Ei. Ma saan aru, et ma ei pidanud oma tehingu lõppu vastu, nii et ma hüvitan teile selle.

Rocco: Mida sa räägid?

Paulie: Mul on homme selleks kellaajaks teie 5000 dollarit, millele lisandub veel 500 dollarit selle eest, et peate veel ühe päeva ootama.

Rocco: Tehing.  Ma tulen seekord homme tagasi.

(südame heli, mis kukub kurgust)

examples_et.example:
Kohtunik: Kas sa siis tapsid oma majaomaniku või mitte?

Kirk: Ma kaklesin temaga.
examples_et.explanation: Siin on klassikaline juhtum, kus oodatakse "jah" või "ei" vastust ja ainsat vastuvõetavat vastust sellisele küsimusele, kuid Kirk lükkab küsimuse kõrvale, pakkudes kolmanda vastusevarianti, mis jätab esialgse küsimuse vastuseta.
